key_insight: 2D/3D perovskite band alignment is highly surface- and composition-dependent, so interface chemistry strongly controls energy-level matching and passivation behavior.
engineering_relevance: Designing stable, efficient perovskite solar cells requires engineering the interface termination and ionic composition, not just the bulk absorber.
method: Atomistic first-principles simulations with hybrid functionals
Computed work function, electron affinity, and band offsets across 2D/3D interfaces
Compared cleaved surfaces and interface terminations for (PEA)2PbI4 on complex 3D perovskites
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preliminary calculations showing work functions, band offsets, and interface electrostatic slopes vary substantially with surface cleavage, termination, and ionic substitution.
watch_item: The results are preliminary and appear sensitive to model termination and compositional assumptions, so experimental validation is still needed before design rules are generalized.
paper_title: Material chemical composition impacts on the band alignments: preliminary results on the 3D/2D perovskite interfaces
